behaviors.behavior: AC-1 triage_gc --apply reports an uncommitted compaction, naming the state, the consequence and a runnable remedy; and stays silent when there was nothing to compact
AC-1 an UNCONFIRMED git state still warns after a rewrite (lines were removed, so silence would hide the divergence), while a non-git directory does not (nothing tracks the log there)
AC-2 --commit folds the compaction so plan_main_tracked_drift returns no_drift afterwards
AC-2 all three main-tree guards plus the path-clean precondition are evaluated BEFORE the destructive rewrite: each refuses with rc 2 and leaves the log byte-unchanged
AC-2 commit_compaction re-checks the git state itself rather than trusting the caller's earlier preflight, so a HEAD that detaches in between cannot yield a commit on a dangling ref
behaviors.evidence: test_triage_gc_publish.py::test_commit_compaction_reguards_itself PASSED; ::test_a_failed_commit_exits_nonzero PASSED (asserts the re-check actually ran)

behaviors.behavior: AC-2 --commit refuses when the log moved after the compaction, refuses outside the main repo root, requires --apply, and exits non-zero when the commit did not happen
AC-3 the .bak is byte-identical to the log it backs up, for LF and for CRLF, and the published log is LF on every platform
behaviors.evidence: test_triage_gc_durability.py::test_backup_is_byte_identical_to_what_it_backs_up PASSED; ::test_backup_preserves_crlf_too PASSED; ::test_the_published_log_is_written_with_LF_on_every_platform PASSED (first two RED against the pre-fix write path)

behaviors.behavior: AC-3 both writes go through durable_atomic_write, and the backup + compaction input derive from ONE read of the source bytes
AC-3 apply_gc refuses to publish when the tracked log changed under the lock, and that refusal leaves no .bak for a compaction that never happened
behaviors.evidence: test_triage_gc_durability.py::test_refuses_to_publish_when_the_log_moved_under_the_lock PASSED (RED pre-fix; injection sits at the last hook before the fingerprint check)

behaviors.behavior: AC-3 a backup-write failure, a publish failure, malformed JSON and undecodable bytes each leave the live log untouched with no temp residue
AC-3 apply_gc keeps its historical return while apply_gc_reporting additionally exposes the bytes it published
AC-4 a definitively failed reconcile commit rolls the dedup rewrite back, leaving the sweep usable — and the state it prevents is pinned directly
AC-4 rollback is refused when another writer appended or when HEAD moved; a timeout does not roll back; a run with no rewrite has nothing to undo; and a failed commit leaves the index clean
AC-5 same-id appends agreeing on the identity anchor collapse keep-last (ADR-163) and report the drop

AC-5 the anchor is compared as a normalised INSTANT: the two ISO-8601 spellings of one moment collapse, a one-microsecond difference still collides, and an unparseable anchor falls back to string equality in both directions
AC-5 anything short of a positive anchor match keeps EVERY line and warns naming triage_repair.py — disagreeing, mixed presence, absent, empty, whitespace-only, and non-str
AC-5 three-plus same-id appends are grouped by exact anchor, not walked pairwise, so no transitive match can drop an unagreed record
AC-5 byte-identical collapse, append+status id sharing, unparseable lines, non-str ids and distinct ids are untouched and never warn
AC-5 the premise the anchor rule rests on (every real append carries originalTs) is pinned against triage.py's source so it cannot rot silently
AC-6 reconcile_main_triage carries the dedup warnings on its result instead of discarding them
AC-6/R1 a benign keep-last collapse leaves the quarantine decision CLEAN and carries the warning — a warning never blocks delivery; only a retained collision does, and it says why
AC-7 an append landing in the restore window is preserved by the salvage rename and adopted into the outbox; a clean restore removes the salvage; adoption is idempotent across a replay
behaviors.evidence: test_sweep_drift_restore.py::test_late_append_is_recovered_instead_of_destroyed PASSED; ::test_clean_restore_leaves_no_salvage_behind PASSED; ::test_late_append_adoption_is_idempotent PASSED; negative control ::test_a_bare_checkout_destroys_a_late_append PASSED

behaviors.behavior: AC-7 salvage content that is not a well-formed append-only suffix is preserved for review, never adopted — unparseable, a wholesale rewrite, or unclassifiable because the read itself failed
AC-7 a failed rename aborts the restore rather than falling back to the overwrite it prevents; a failed checkout puts the log back only when the path is absent, otherwise BOTH artifacts are kept
behaviors.evidence: test_sweep_drift_restore_faults.py::test_rename_failure_aborts_instead_of_overwriting PASSED; ::test_checkout_failure_puts_the_log_back PASSED; ::test_checkout_failure_with_a_reappeared_file_keeps_both PASSED (the first two assert a `fired` tripwire so the injection cannot silently miss)

behaviors.behavior: AC-7 a MISSING tracked log after a failed put-back returns error, not the soft buffered, and the sweep stops on it
AC-7 the salvage pointer is repeated on every SUBSEQUENT main_tracked_diverged refusal, not only at the instant of failure
AC-7 salvage names are exclusive, and the salvage path is gitignored by the SHIPPED template (every adopter, not just this repo)
behaviors.evidence: test_sweep_drift_restore.py::test_salvage_names_are_exclusive PASSED; ::test_salvage_path_is_gitignored_by_the_shipped_template PASSED (with a control that the tracked log itself is NOT ignored)

behaviors.behavior: AC-8 the four components compose on a real git repo: GC leaves the channel dead and says so, --commit keeps it alive, main-tree drift is adopted with a late append salvaged and delivered by the next sweep, a failed reconcile commit leaves the sweep usable, an id collision blocks loudly without deleting a record, and a benign refresh still delivers
R8 every moved name resolves from BOTH its old and new home as the same object, and each of the twelve modules imports alone in a fresh interpreter (circular-import guard)
the GC vocabulary drift guard still excludes the module that DEFINES MACHINE_REASONS after the extraction, resolved from the module object rather than a filename
behaviors.evidence: test_triage_gc_vocab_drift.py — 4 tests PASSED (the filename-based exclusion broke on the move and was caught by test_legacy_retained_tokens_have_no_live_emitter)

surface_verification.detail: triage_gc's CLI is a real behaviour surface this change alters (new --commit flag, new rc 2/3 exit codes, new operator-facing warning text), so surface=cli rather than none. The runner drives main() end to end plus the cross-component composition test against real git repos.
